subject: Greenlight criteria and fallback playbook for evaluation
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Kerr <samantha.kerr@epsilonhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Greenlight criteria and fallback playbook for evaluation

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the productive kickoff this morning. As discussed, we pulled together a compact set of quantifiable success criteria and a minimal fallback plan so the pilot can proceed without surprises. Please see the summary below and confirm anything that needs to change before we lock the MAP and hand off to your procurement team. I attached the working MAP workbook and a short smoke-test spec.

Primary success criteria (must hit all for greenlight):
- P95 inference latency for 512-token requests: < 350 ms in your us-west region (measured over a 24h window)
- Top-line concordance: >= 92% on the curated clinical prompt set (200 prompts)
- Quality regression: no more than 1% drop vs baseline on the key 20 clinical prompts after model patching
- End-to-end throughput: sustain 40 rps peak with <= 5% tail latency slippage for 1 hour stress window
- Security & compliance: SOC2 evidence review complete; ability to meet your data-retention policy (90 days)

Exit gates (fail-fast conditions):
- If P95 > 600 ms for > 2 consecutive hours during peak test window -> trigger rollback to baseline model and start post-mortem
- If concordance < 85% on any daily evaluation -> pause feature ramp and escalate to ML lead
- Any unresolved PII handling discrepancy flagged by your security team -> stop ingest and remediate

Acceptance tests (deliverables we’ll run together):
1) Smoke suite (attached): 30 canonical prompts, pass threshold 28/30
2) Load trial: 1-hour ramp to 40 rps with telemetry capture (we provide dashboard)
3) Regression harness: automated nightly check comparing commit X to baseline on 200 prompts
4) Integration sanity: end-to-end flow test with your staging dataset (sample redaction validation)

Timeline proposal (high level):
- May 21: finalize MAP workbook + sign-off on SOW (you/Procurement)
- May 24–26: staging integration and smoke tests
- May 27: load trial and acceptance window begins (48 hours)
- May 29: decision checkpoint — either greenlight to proceed to pilot expansion or remediation plan starts

Action items for Epsilon:
- Confirm SOC2 evidence owner and target date for docs (procurement/contact)
- Confirm the 20 clinical-priority prompts redaction list by EOD May 21

If this looks good I’ll send the MAP workbook and a short one-pager for Procurement to speed review.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Samantha Kerr <samantha.kerr@epsilonhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 13:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Greenlight criteria and fallback playbook for evaluation

Marissa —

Appreciate the clear breakdown, this is very helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

- Concordance metric: when you say 92% on the 200 prompts, can you confirm whether that’s exact-match or clinically-relevant threshold (we prefer clinically-relevant; i.e., semantic match assessed by two clinicians)
- Latency: the 350 ms P95 target is acceptable if we exclude the client-side post-processing step; please call that out in the MAP so procurement understands the scope
- Data retention: procurement may ask for a 180-day option; can you note if that is feasible and any cost delta?

We will:
- Share SOC2 contact (procurement@epsilonhealth.com) and target doc handoff May 24
- Finalize the priority 20 prompts by close of business May 21 (Dr. Patel will own)

We agree to the proposed timeline but would like a one-day buffer before the May 27 load if the staging integration uncovers anything. Can we build one contingency day into the MAP?

Thanks,
Samantha Kerr
Director, Digital Products | Epsilon Health
samantha.kerr@epsilonhealth.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Greenlight criteria and fallback playbook for evaluation

Forwarding Epsilon's clarifying notes — 3 quick updates to the workbook before I send to Procurement:

1) Concordance definition: switch to clinician-reviewed semantic match (two-reviewer tie-break) — affects evaluation harness labeling (we need to add reviewer fields).
2) Latency note: call out that P95 excludes client post-processing; update the acceptance test wording and the dashboard label.
3) Data retention: procurement asked about 180-day option — estimate delta is ~+12% on storage/costs for the pilot; annotate costs in the MAP and highlight as optional add-on.

Planned deliverables from us tonight: updated MAP workbook, revised smoke-tests doc, and a one‑page for Procurement summarizing SLOs and optional 180-day retention cost. I included the Drive link and DocuSign URL in metadata.

Can you take the lead on the cost delta calc, Ben? Mina — want you to validate the clinician-review workflow changes and ensure the harness can accept dual reviewer labels.

Marissa
